rv.q: Meanwhile, “Slave Play” makes a kind of history of its own, boldly bringing Broadway into unfamiliar waters!
The two-hour no intermission play, although unequivocally satirical in its presentation and performance, could be rough going for many even as it presents a challenge for the easily receptive.

cn.t: Harris' provocative exploration of race and sexuality divides critics, with praise for its audacious concept and strong performances but questions about its execution and therapeutic framework's effectiveness.

vs.sum: The August Wilson Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, although the rake isn't steep, which can cause issues if seated behind taller patrons. The theater has average comfort with decent legroom but tight seats. Its Italian-inspired design and cozy feel enhance the ambiance, making it a pleasant venue overall. Facilities are adequate, with standard amenities and helpful staff.

acc.note: Stair lift to orchestra; elevator between orchestra and mezzanine. Infrared headsets available.
